5. Mr. Fazlul Karim, learned Advocate appearing with Mr. Mir Hashmat Ali, Mr. Rezbabul Kabir and Mr. Khandakar Arninul Huq, learned Advocates for the petitioner submits that the Electoral Rolls Rules, 1982 prepared under the Electoral Ordinance, 1982 has a presumption of correctness in law. He submits that section 17 of the said Ordinance clearly bars the jurisdiction of court to question the validity of the electoral rolls prepared under the Ordinance or the legality or the propriety of any proceedings or action taken thereunder by or under the authority of the commission or the Registration Officer and in the voters list which was prepared under the Electoral Rolls Rules, 1982 and marked as Exhibit 'E', the age of the present petitioner having been shown as 25 years, the said entry could not be challenged and, as such, the Appellate Tribunal committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in holding that the present-petitioner failed to prove that he attained the age of 25 years. In support of his contention Mr. Fazlul Karim has referred the case of Hari Prasad Mulshankar Trivedi vs VB Raju and others reported in AIR 1973 (SC) 2602 and also the case of Kabul Singh Appellant vs Kundan Singh and others reported in AIR 1970 (SC) 340. 

 6. Mr. Md. Serajul Hoque, learned Advocate appearing for the Election Petitioner (opposite party No. I in this Rule), on the other hand, submits that the entry made in the voters list prepared under the Electoral Rolls Rules is not final and conclusive and there is no presumption of correctness and the same can very much be challenged before the Tribunal. Mr. serajul Haque, in support of his contention, has referred the case of Major Ali Akbar Chowdhury vs Sayeedur Rahman and 4 others reported in 15 DLR 153 and the case of Muhammad Yousuf vs Malik Karam Dad Khan reported in 20 DLR (WP) 33.
